reviews.title: Great value. Handles higher speed than advertised. Cosmetically pleasing.
reviews.comment:
Quite happy. I typically stick with gskill. I used to push memory for oc leader boards but I haven’t in a while. I bought these for a sim rig and did a simple 6800-7000mt/s overclock. Without the best cooling. Low quality board. Intel cpu. No crashes in a week and I’ve only rebooted once. They seem to handle higher speeds well. And even though gskill is still my go to (I bought these as they were cheaper and same day delivery) I was quite happy with them. Cosmetically they look nice as well. This and a cheap phantom cpu cooler got us a decent 15-22% fps increase with cutting out our random frame stutter from the premade pc that came with the sim rig from cyberpowerpc. Who thought a single dim stick was a good install idea… especially for a 3x 1080p 165hz setup.
The manufacture should send us more products to test. We have used quite a few of their products for other projects and I’m happy to see the quality improving.

reviews.title: The best RAM sticks I've ever owned
reviews.comment:
Update:
I paid around 125 bucks for this ONE MONTH ago.
The prices are insane for GDDR5 now. Sorry folks.
-
Finally got my hands on some of the best RAM in the business.
Not disappointed so far. Speeds are stable, compatible with my board, and lighting looks great, even with the PC sleeping.
Some well built hardware
Only issue is the software. Version 5 wouldn't detect the sticks but version 4 does.
It also had a conflict with OpenRGB until I removed them from the settings.
Another positive is that the RGB colors/effects are saved onboard and don't require any software to run in the background on Windows. Something you have to look out for these days.
Made in Taiwan
